title: A follow-up on the same review delegation replaces the only parent-visible structured result of the earlier attempt
outcome: When a parent sends a follow-up to a completed read-only review delegation, the earlier attempt's authoritative structured result (packet, result, raw page) stays retrievable by the parent, for example through termal_get_session_result with an attempt selector or a distinct per-attempt result id. A later attempt does not replace the only parent-visible copy. Producer guidance makes per-attempt immutable export the default, so an in-place overwrite of an archive cannot silently destroy cited evidence.
acceptance: After a same-delegation follow-up, the parent can retrieve each retained terminal review attempt's structured result and paged output by attempt plus immutable resultId. A repaired terminal cut of the same attempt receives a distinct resultId; previously published ids remain unchanged. Attempt-only selection returns the latest confirmed version and its resultId; all subsequent pages and exports pin that identity. Concurrent newer attempts cannot alter or mix those views, and default current-attempt behavior remains documented.

Historical retrieval enforces existing parent/delegation authorization and validated attempt provenance, never promotes old truth into the active attempt or changes its waits/lifecycle; unavailable or corrupt history is explicit and never substituted with another attempt.

Scripted follow-up, retry and real-persistence restart/failure witnesses prove earlier result/output custody, stable paging and bounded-capacity refusal without silent loss; legacy missing history is reported honestly, not reconstructed as authoritative from a newer transcript.

The standard export path/guidance preserves distinct immutable per-attempt artifacts and manifests, rejects differing overwrite, and demonstrates that a second export leaves the first cited packet and page hashes unchanged.
